THE LAST FOUR OFFENDERS IN webclient/. 81 -> 77, and the directory is now clear.

  action_state.js         getActionParams              97 -> under 80
  controller_component.js makeControllerComponent      93 -> under 80
  profiling_qweb.js       renderProfilingInformation  100 -> under 80
  profiling_qweb.js       its forEach callback         90 -> under 80

The last two are one unit: the method was a `forEach` over ace's tokens with a
four-branch ladder inside it, so the gate counted the method and the callback
separately and splitting the ladder cleared both. Each branch is now named for
the token it handles -- `_popOnEndTagClose`, `_popOnEndTagOpen`,
`_annotateDirective`, `_openTag` -- and the callback reads as the dispatch it
always was. `_openTag` returns the extended xpath rather than assigning a
captured `let`, which is what made the old body hard to follow: three of the four
branches leave xpath alone and the fourth rewrites it in the middle.

`getActionParams` was three independent resolutions -- url names an action, url
names a model, url names neither -- sharing one accumulator. `resolveActionFromKey`
and `resolveActionFromModel` now own the first two, with `buildActiveContext` and
`storedActionAnswersTo` naming the two conditions that were written inline. The
model branch keeps its asymmetry and now says why: a record reopens as a bare form
because the id identifies it, a multi-record view does not because rebuilding one
without the original domain would show a wider set than the url meant.

`makeControllerComponent` is a factory whose body is a class, so the length was
the class, not a function doing too much. `useControllerStateRecorders` takes the
one part that is genuinely conditional -- the three CallbackRecorders a non-dialog
controller exposes, and the `View` exception that takes them as props instead of
through the sub-env.
